evals.prompt: Train the confirmed Kumo churn model (model_plan, training_table and snapshot are ready in my Snowflake notebook) and publish it to the model registry in ML.REGISTRY as CHURN_MODEL version V3.
evals.expected_output: Publishes during the fit: `trainer.fit(training_table, snapshot=snapshot, export_config=kumo.ModelOutputConfig(connector=registry_connector, location=kumo.ModelRegistryLocation(model_name='CHURN_MODEL', version='V3')))` with a connector scoped to ML.REGISTRY, then checks `training_result.published_model` and raises if it is None. Uses `location`, not `path`, for Snowflake. Checks that V3 does not already exist first and does not overwrite an existing version.
assertions: Passes a kumo.ModelOutputConfig as export_config to trainer.fit
Uses kumo.ModelRegistryLocation with model_name CHURN_MODEL and version V3
Uses location= rather than path= for the Snowflake registry
Checks training_result.published_model and treats None as a failure
Checks that version V3 does not already exist and does not overwrite an existing version

evals.prompt: Load CHURN_MODEL from our Snowflake model registry in ML.REGISTRY and score new customers. SHOW VERSIONS lists V1, V2 and V3.
evals.expected_output: Several versions exist and the user named none, so it asks which version to load rather than choosing one. It explains that `version=None` loads the registry default, which is not necessarily the newest, and that 'latest' would mean the newest created_on, passed explicitly. It does not retrain.
assertions: Asks which version to load instead of picking one
Explains that loading without a version uses the registry default, not necessarily the newest
Does not train a new model

evals.prompt: Load version V2 of CHURN_MODEL from the Snowflake registry ML.REGISTRY and score our customers as of 2026-12-01. The graph-building code and query are in our training record for V2.
evals.expected_output: Restores with `kumo.Trainer.load_from_connector(registry_connector, location=kumo.ModelRegistryLocation(model_name='CHURN_MODEL', version='V2'))`, rebuilds the graph from the V2 training record (not the live schema), creates a fresh `graph.snapshot()`, generates the prediction table with a naive `prediction_time` and `plan=loaded.training_table_generation_plan`, and predicts with `snapshot=` and an explicit binary threshold. No retraining.
assertions: Loads with kumo.Trainer.load_from_connector and an explicit ModelRegistryLocation for version V2
Rebuilds the graph from the V2 training record rather than from the live schema or another version
Builds a new graph.snapshot() for scoring
Passes plan=loaded.training_table_generation_plan to generate_prediction_table
Passes snapshot= to predict and an explicit binary classification threshold
Does not call fit

evals.prompt: Before this Snowflake notebook shuts down, keep my Kumo run's aggregate metrics and the per-trial validation results on the internal stage @ML.ARTIFACTS so I can look at them next week.
evals.expected_output: Selects explicit files from one run (not the whole scratch tree, which can hold source data and credentials), writes aggregate metrics to a new JSON file with allow_nan=False, builds an archive with the packaged `create_archive` helper from an explicit list of relative paths, uploads with `session.file.put(..., auto_compress=False, overwrite=False)` to a new run-specific prefix and checks exactly one `UPLOADED` result, and records the stage path and archive SHA256 digest.
assertions: Selects explicit files from one run instead of uploading the whole scratch directory
Uses the packaged create_archive helper with a list of explicit relative file paths
Uploads with session.file.put and overwrite=False
Checks that the upload status is UPLOADED and treats anything else, including SKIPPED, as not retained
Records the stage object path and the archive digest

evals.prompt: Look up my Kumo model by its hosted job ID job-8841 and redeploy it.
evals.expected_output: The local Kumo API has no hosted model or job ID lookup. It says so and asks for the registry model name and version, or a retained bundle, instead of inventing a lookup.
assertions: Says there is no hosted model or job ID lookup in this local API
Asks for a registry model and explicit version, or a retained bundle
Does not invent an API call that fetches a model by job ID

evals.prompt: Save my trained scikit-learn model with joblib and upload it to s3://ml-models/fraud/.
evals.expected_output: A scikit-learn persistence task unrelated to Kumo. The agent answers with joblib and an S3 upload, without loading the Kumo persistence skill.
assertions: Does not load or follow the kumo-model-persistence skill
Uses joblib to save the model and uploads it to the S3 path
